title: Chapter 4: RAG — Chat with Your Own Documents
content:
Chapter 4: RAG — Chat with Your Own Documents

Opening Hook: The Moment AI Becomes Useful for Your Files

A normal AI assistant can answer general questions.

But what happens when you ask:

What does my PDF say about refunds?

or:

Summarize the onboarding document I uploaded.

or:

Find the section that explains the cancellation policy.

A general model may not know your document.

It may guess.

It may answer from general knowledge.

It may sound confident even when the answer is not in your file.

That is not good enough for serious AI applications.

This is where RAG becomes important.

RAG stands for:

Retrieval-Augmented Generation

The idea is simple:

First retrieve relevant information. Then ask the AI model to answer using that information.

Instead of asking the model to answer from memory, you give it context from your own documents.

This chapter teaches one of the most important skills in practical AI development:

How to build an assistant that answers questions using your own files.

You will build your first flagship project:

Personal Document AI Assistant

It will read a PDF, split the text into chunks, retrieve the most relevant chunks for a question, and ask the model to answer using only that retrieved context.

This is the foundation behind many real-world AI products:

  • Chat with PDF apps
  • Company knowledge assistants
  • Internal documentation bots
  • Legal document helpers
  • Student study assistants
  • Customer support knowledge bots
  • Research assistants
  • Business document search tools

By the end of this chapter, your AI assistant will no longer be limited to general knowledge.

It will be able to work with your documents.

What You Will Learn

By the end of this chapter, you will understand:

  • What RAG is
  • Why RAG matters
  • Why RAG can reduce hallucinations
  • How document question-answering works
  • How to extract text from PDFs
  • How to split text into chunks
  • How simple retrieval works
  • How to inject retrieved context into a prompt
  • How to make the model say “not found” when context is missing
  • How to test RAG helper functions without live API calls
  • How to build a PDF question-answering assistant in Python
  • How this project becomes a portfolio or freelance asset

Why This Chapter Matters

In earlier chapters, your assistant used only the user’s prompt and the model’s general ability.

That is useful for general tasks.

But many valuable AI applications need private or specific information.

For example:

Company policy documents Course notes Technical manuals Client files Research papers Product documentation Contracts Reports Training material

The model may not know these documents.

Even if the model has broad knowledge, it should not guess what your document says.

RAG gives your app a way to ground answers in provided material.

A RAG assistant follows this pattern:

User question ↓ Search relevant document chunks ↓ Insert chunks into prompt ↓ Ask model to answer using context ↓ Return answer

This makes AI apps more useful and more trustworthy.

RAG does not make hallucinations impossible.

But it gives the model relevant context and gives your app a way to say:

I could not find that in the document.

That is a major improvement.

4.1 What Is RAG?

RAG stands for Retrieval-Augmented Generation.

It has two main parts.

Retrieval

Retrieval means finding relevant information.

In this chapter, your app will retrieve chunks from a PDF.

Example:

Question: What is the refund period? Retrieved chunk: Customers may request a refund within 30 days of purchase.

Generation

Generation means asking the model to produce an answer.

But instead of asking the model from general memory, you give it the retrieved chunk.

Example prompt:

Use only this context to answer the question. Context: Customers may request a refund within 30 days of purchase. Question: What is the refund period?

The model can now answer:

The refund period is 30 days after purchase.

That is RAG.

4.2 Why RAG Reduces Hallucinations

A hallucination happens when the model produces an answer that is unsupported, misleading, or false.

Example:

Question: What is the refund period? Bad answer: The refund period is 90 days.

If the document says 30 days, this is wrong.

RAG reduces this risk by giving the model relevant context and instructing it to use only that context.

A good RAG prompt says:

Use only the provided context. If the answer is not in the context, say you could not find it. Do not invent facts.

This does not guarantee perfection.

But it gives your app a stronger foundation.

The model is less likely to guess when it has relevant text and strict instructions.

4.3 The Basic RAG Pipeline

A beginner-friendly RAG pipeline looks like this:

PDF file ↓ Extract text ↓ Split text into chunks ↓ Store chunks in memory ↓ User asks question ↓ Retrieve relevant chunks ↓ Build prompt with context ↓ LLM generates answer

In this chapter, you will use a simple keyword-based retriever.

In Chapter 5, you will upgrade the retrieval layer with embeddings, vector databases, and semantic search.

That is intentional.

First, learn the RAG flow.

Then improve retrieval quality.

4.4 Why Chunking Matters

Most documents are too large to send fully to a model every time.

Even if a model can accept long input, sending the entire document can be:

  • Slower
  • More expensive
  • Less focused
  • Harder to debug
  • More likely to include irrelevant text

Chunking solves this by splitting the document into smaller pieces.

Example:

Full document ↓ Chunk 1 Chunk 2 Chunk 3 Chunk 4

When the user asks a question, the app retrieves only the most relevant chunks.

Better context usually leads to better answers.

4.5 What Makes RAG Different from Search?

Search finds information.

RAG finds information and then asks the model to explain or answer using it.

Search result:

Refunds are available within 30 days.

RAG answer:

According to the document, customers can request a refund within 30 days of purchase.

The retrieval step finds the evidence.

The generation step turns the evidence into a helpful answer.

4.6 What This Chapter Will Not Do Yet

This chapter will not use vector databases yet.

It will not use embeddings yet.

It will not build a web app yet.

It will not handle scanned PDFs with OCR.

It will not guarantee perfect answers.

Those features come later or require additional tools.

This chapter focuses on the core RAG idea:

retrieve relevant context + generate an answer from that context

Once you understand this, embeddings and vector databases will make much more sense in Chapter 5.

4.7 Project: Personal Document AI Assistant

What This Project Does

This project builds a PDF question-answering assistant.

The user provides a PDF file path.

The app extracts the PDF text, splits it into chunks, and waits for questions.

The user can ask:

What is this document about?

or:

What are the main requirements?

or:

Does the document mention refunds?

The app retrieves relevant chunks and asks the model to answer using them.

Who This Helps

This project helps:

  • Students studying PDFs
  • Freelancers reviewing client documents
  • Developers building RAG apps
  • Professionals searching reports
  • Entrepreneurs prototyping document assistants
  • Anyone who wants to chat with their own files

What You Will Build

Create this project structure:

chapter_04_pdf_rag_assistant/ sample_docs/ .env.example .gitignore requirements.txt llm_client.py pdf_loader.py text_utils.py retriever.py rag_assistant.py app.py test_text_utils.py test_retriever.py test_rag_assistant.py README.md

4.8 Setup

Step 1: Create the Folder

mkdir chapter_04_pdf_rag_assistant cd chapter_04_pdf_rag_assistant mkdir sample_docs

Step 2: Create a Virtual Environment

python -m venv .venv

Activate it.

On macOS or Linux:

source .venv/bin/activate

On Windows PowerShell:

.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

Step 3: Create requirements.txt

openai python-dotenv pypdf pytest

Install dependencies:

pip install -r requirements.txt

Step 4: Create .env.example

OPENAI_API_KEY=replace_with_your_api_key OPENAI_MODEL=gpt-4.1-mini OPENAI_TEMPERATURE=0.2

Copy it to .env.

On macOS or Linux:

cp .env.example .env

On Windows PowerShell:

Copy-Item .env.example .env

Then edit .env and add your real API key.

Never publish your real .env file.

4.9 File: .gitignore

Create .gitignore:

.env .venv/ __pycache__/ .pytest_cache/ *.pyc *.log outputs/

This keeps secrets and local files out of version control.

4.10 File: llm_client.py

This is the reusable LLM client pattern from earlier chapters.

Create llm_client.py:

""" Reusable LLM client for Chapter 4. This module keeps provider-specific model calls separate from RAG logic. """ import os from dataclasses import dataclass, field from typing import Protocol from dotenv import load_dotenv from openai import OpenAI load_dotenv() def get_env_float(name: str, default: float) -> float: """Read a float from an environment variable safely.""" raw_value = os.getenv(name) if raw_value is None: return default try: return float(raw_value) except ValueError: return default @dataclass class LLMConfig: """Configuration for the LLM client.""" model: str = field( default_factory=lambda: os.getenv("OPENAI_MODEL", "gpt-4.1-mini") ) temperature: float = field( default_factory=lambda: get_env_float("OPENAI_TEMPERATURE", 0.2) ) class LLMProvider(Protocol): """Protocol for LLM-like clients.""" def complete(self, system: str, user: str) -> str: """Return model-generated text.""" ... class LLMClient: """Reusable client for sending prompts to an LLM.""" def __init__(self, config: LLMConfig | None = None): self.config = config or LLMConfig() api_key = os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY") if not api_key: raise ValueError( "OPENAI_API_KEY is missing. Add it to your .env file." ) self.client = OpenAI(api_key=api_key) def build_input(self, system: str, user: str) -> str: """Combine system and user messages into model input.""" if not system.strip(): raise ValueError("System instruction cannot be empty.") if not user.strip(): raise ValueError("User request cannot be empty.") return f""" System instruction: {system.strip()} User request: {user.strip()} """ def complete(self, system: str, user: str) -> str: """Send a request to the model and return text output.""" model_input = self.build_input(system=system, user=user) response = self.client.responses.create( model=self.config.model, input=model_input, temperature=self.config.temperature, ) return response.output_text class MockLLMClient: """Mock client for tests.""" def __init__(self, response_text: str = "Mock answer"): self.response_text = response_text self.calls: list[dict[str, str]] = [] def complete(self, system: str, user: str) -> str: """Return a fixed response and record the call.""" if not system.strip(): raise ValueError("System instruction cannot be empty.") if not user.strip(): raise ValueError("User request cannot be empty.") self.calls.append( { "system": system, "user": user, } ) return self.response_text Not executed automatically: requires live API credentials, network access, or external service.

4.11 File: pdf_loader.py

This file extracts text from a PDF.

Create pdf_loader.py:

""" PDF loading utilities for the Chapter 4 RAG assistant. """ from pathlib import Path from pypdf import PdfReader def load_pdf_text(pdf_path: str) -> str: """ Extract text from a PDF file. Args: pdf_path: Path to the PDF file. Returns: Extracted text with page labels. Raises: FileNotFoundError: If the PDF does not exist. ValueError: If no extractable text is found. """ path = Path(pdf_path) if not path.exists(): raise FileNotFoundError(f"PDF file not found: {pdf_path}") if path.suffix.lower() != ".pdf": raise ValueError("File must be a PDF.") reader = PdfReader(str(path)) page_texts = [] for page_number, page in enumerate(reader.pages, start=1): text = page.extract_text() or "" if text.strip(): page_texts.append(f"[Page {page_number}]\n{text.strip()}") if not page_texts: raise ValueError( "No extractable text found. This PDF may be scanned or image-based." ) return "\n\n".join(page_texts) Test result: Python syntax check passed.

Important Note About Scanned PDFs

Some PDFs are images of pages rather than real text.

This project uses normal text extraction.

If a PDF is scanned or image-based, you may need OCR.

OCR is outside the scope of this chapter.

4.12 File: text_utils.py

This file cleans and chunks text.

Create text_utils.py:

""" Text utilities for the Chapter 4 RAG assistant. """ def clean_text(text: str) -> str: """ Normalize whitespace while preserving readable text. """ return " ".join(text.split()) def chunk_text( text: str, chunk_size: int = 1000, overlap: int = 150, ) -> list[str]: """ Split text into overlapping chunks. Args: text: Text to split. chunk_size: Maximum number of characters per chunk. overlap: Number of characters repeated between chunks. Returns: List of text chunks. """ if chunk_size <= 0: raise ValueError("chunk_size must be greater than 0.") if overlap < 0: raise ValueError("overlap cannot be negative.") if overlap >= chunk_size: raise ValueError("overlap must be smaller than chunk_size.") cleaned = clean_text(text) if not cleaned: return [] chunks = [] start = 0 while start < len(cleaned): end = start + chunk_size chunk = cleaned[start:end].strip() if chunk: chunks.append(chunk) start = end - overlap return chunks def preview_text(text: str, max_chars: int = 500) -> str: """ Return a short preview of text. """ cleaned = clean_text(text) if len(cleaned) <= max_chars: return cleaned return cleaned[:max_chars].rstrip() + "..." Test result: Python syntax check passed.

4.13 File: retriever.py

This file retrieves chunks using simple keyword overlap.

This is not as strong as embeddings, but it is good for learning the RAG flow.

Create retriever.py:

""" Simple retrieval utilities for the Chapter 4 RAG assistant. This chapter uses keyword overlap retrieval for clarity. Chapter 5 upgrades retrieval with embeddings and vector databases. """ import re def tokenize(text: str) -> set[str]: """ Convert text into a set of lowercase search terms. """ words = re.findall(r"[a-zA-Z0-9]+", text.lower()) return { word for word in words if len(word) > 2 } def score_chunk(question: str, chunk: str) -> int: """ Score a chunk by keyword overlap with the question. """ question_terms = tokenize(question) chunk_terms = tokenize(chunk) return len(question_terms.intersection(chunk_terms)) def retrieve_relevant_chunks( question: str, chunks: list[str], top_k: int = 4, ) -> list[str]: """ Retrieve the most relevant chunks for a question. """ if not question.strip(): raise ValueError("Question cannot be empty.") if top_k <= 0: raise ValueError("top_k must be greater than 0.") scored_chunks = [ (score_chunk(question, chunk), chunk) for chunk in chunks ] scored_chunks.sort(key=lambda item: item[0], reverse=True) selected = [ chunk for score, chunk in scored_chunks[:top_k] if score > 0 ] if not selected and chunks: selected = chunks[:1] return selected def format_context(chunks: list[str]) -> str: """ Format retrieved chunks for a RAG prompt. """ if not chunks: return "No relevant context found." context_blocks = [] for index, chunk in enumerate(chunks, start=1): context_blocks.append(f"[Context {index}]\n{chunk}") return "\n\n".join(context_blocks) Test result: Python syntax check passed.

4.14 File: rag_assistant.py

This file builds the RAG prompt and calls the LLM.

Create rag_assistant.py:

""" RAG assistant logic for Chapter 4. The assistant answers questions using retrieved document context. """ from llm_client import LLMClient, LLMProvider from retriever import retrieve_relevant_chunks, format_context RAG_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """ You are a careful document question-answering assistant. Rules: - Use only the provided document context. - If the answer is not in the context, say: "I could not find that in the document." - Do not invent facts. - Do not use outside knowledge unless the user explicitly asks for general background. - Keep the answer clear and practical. - Mention when the answer is based on limited context. """ def build_rag_prompt(question: str, context: str) -> str: """ Build a RAG prompt using the question and retrieved context. """ if not question.strip(): raise ValueError("Question cannot be empty.") if not context.strip(): raise ValueError("Context cannot be empty.") return f""" Document context: {context} Question: {question} Answer the question using only the document context. If the answer is not present, say: "I could not find that in the document." Return: Answer: A clear answer based on the context. Evidence: Briefly mention which part of the context supports the answer. Limitations: Mention if the context is incomplete or does not answer the question. """ def answer_question_from_chunks( question: str, chunks: list[str], client: LLMProvider | None = None, top_k: int = 4, ) -> str: """ Retrieve relevant chunks and answer the question using an LLM. """ if not chunks: return "No document chunks are available. Load a document first." relevant_chunks = retrieve_relevant_chunks( question=question, chunks=chunks, top_k=top_k, ) context = format_context(relevant_chunks) prompt = build_rag_prompt(question=question, context=context) llm = client or LLMClient() return llm.complete( system=RAG_SYSTEM_PROMPT, user=prompt, ) def inspect_retrieval(question: str, chunks: list[str], top_k: int = 4) -> str: """ Return retrieved chunks for debugging. """ relevant_chunks = retrieve_relevant_chunks( question=question, chunks=chunks, top_k=top_k, ) return format_context(relevant_chunks) Test result: Python syntax check passed.

4.15 File: app.py

This is the command-line interface.

Create app.py:

""" Chapter 4 Project: Personal Document AI Assistant This app: 1. Loads a PDF 2. Splits it into chunks 3. Lets the user ask questions 4. Retrieves relevant chunks 5. Answers using an LLM """ from pdf_loader import load_pdf_text from text_utils import chunk_text, preview_text from rag_assistant import answer_question_from_chunks, inspect_retrieval def print_welcome() -> None: """Print welcome message.""" print("\nPersonal Document AI Assistant") print("=" * 50) print("Ask questions about a PDF document.") print("Type /exit to quit.") print("Type /inspect [question] to see retrieved context.") print("=" * 50) def load_document_flow() -> list[str]: """ Ask the user for a PDF path and load document chunks. """ pdf_path = input("\nEnter path to PDF file: ").strip() print("\nLoading PDF...") text = load_pdf_text(pdf_path) print("\nDocument preview:") print("-" * 50) print(preview_text(text)) print("-" * 50) chunks = chunk_text(text) print(f"\nLoaded {len(chunks)} chunk(s).") return chunks def main() -> None: """Run the document assistant.""" print_welcome() try: chunks = load_document_flow() except Exception as error: print(f"\nFailed to load document: {error}") return while True: question = input("\nQuestion: ").strip() if question.lower() in {"/exit", "exit", "quit"}: print("Goodbye.") break if not question: print("Please enter a question.") continue if question.startswith("/inspect"): inspect_question = question.replace("/inspect", "", 1).strip() if not inspect_question: print("Please provide a question to inspect.") continue try: print("\nRetrieved context:") print("-" * 50) print(inspect_retrieval(inspect_question, chunks)) print("-" * 50) except Exception as error: print(f"Inspection error: {error}") continue try: answer = answer_question_from_chunks( question=question, chunks=chunks, ) print("\nAssistant:") print(answer) except Exception as error: print(f"\nError: {error}") if __name__ == "__main__": main() Test result: Python syntax check passed.

4.16 File: test_text_utils.py

These tests check text cleaning and chunking.

Create test_text_utils.py:

import pytest from text_utils import clean_text, chunk_text, preview_text def test_clean_text_normalizes_whitespace(): text = "Python is\n\nuseful\tfor AI." result = clean_text(text) assert result == "Python is useful for AI." def test_chunk_text_returns_chunks(): text = "Python is useful for AI. " * 100 chunks = chunk_text(text, chunk_size=100, overlap=20) assert len(chunks) > 1 assert all(len(chunk) <= 100 for chunk in chunks) def test_chunk_text_empty_returns_empty_list(): chunks = chunk_text(" ") assert chunks == [] def test_chunk_text_invalid_chunk_size(): with pytest.raises(ValueError): chunk_text("hello", chunk_size=0) def test_chunk_text_invalid_overlap(): with pytest.raises(ValueError): chunk_text("hello", chunk_size=100, overlap=100) def test_preview_text_short_text(): text = "Short text" assert preview_text(text, max_chars=50) == "Short text" def test_preview_text_long_text(): text = "x" * 100 result = preview_text(text, max_chars=10) assert result == "xxxxxxxxxx..." Test result: Python syntax check passed.

4.17 File: test_retriever.py

These tests check retrieval without calling the model.

Create test_retriever.py:

import pytest from retriever import ( tokenize, score_chunk, retrieve_relevant_chunks, format_context, ) def test_tokenize_returns_terms(): terms = tokenize("Python, AI, and RAG!") assert "python" in terms assert "rag" in terms def test_score_chunk_matches_question_terms(): question = "What is the refund policy?" chunk = "The refund policy allows customers to request refunds." score = score_chunk(question, chunk) assert score > 0 def test_retrieve_relevant_chunks_returns_best_match(): chunks = [ "Python is a programming language.", "Refunds are available within 30 days.", "Bananas are yellow.", ] results = retrieve_relevant_chunks( question="How long do refunds take?", chunks=chunks, top_k=1, ) assert len(results) == 1 assert "Refunds" in results[0] def test_retrieve_relevant_chunks_empty_question(): with pytest.raises(ValueError): retrieve_relevant_chunks("", ["Some chunk"]) def test_retrieve_relevant_chunks_invalid_top_k(): with pytest.raises(ValueError): retrieve_relevant_chunks("question", ["Some chunk"], top_k=0) def test_format_context_with_chunks(): context = format_context(["First chunk", "Second chunk"]) assert "[Context 1]" in context assert "First chunk" in context assert "[Context 2]" in context def test_format_context_without_chunks(): context = format_context([]) assert context == "No relevant context found." Test result: Python syntax check passed.

4.18 File: test_rag_assistant.py

These tests check RAG prompt creation and mock client behavior.

Create test_rag_assistant.py:

import pytest from llm_client import MockLLMClient from rag_assistant import ( build_rag_prompt, answer_question_from_chunks, inspect_retrieval, ) def test_build_rag_prompt_contains_question_and_context(): prompt = build_rag_prompt( question="What is the refund period?", context="Refunds are available within 30 days.", ) assert "What is the refund period?" in prompt assert "Refunds are available within 30 days." in prompt assert "I could not find that in the document" in prompt def test_build_rag_prompt_rejects_empty_question(): with pytest.raises(ValueError): build_rag_prompt("", "Some context") def test_build_rag_prompt_rejects_empty_context(): with pytest.raises(ValueError): build_rag_prompt("Question?", "") def test_answer_question_from_chunks_with_mock_client(): chunks = [ "Refunds are available within 30 days.", "Shipping takes 5 business days.", ] mock = MockLLMClient(response_text="Mock RAG answer") answer = answer_question_from_chunks( question="What is the refund period?", chunks=chunks, client=mock, top_k=1, ) assert answer == "Mock RAG answer" assert len(mock.calls) == 1 assert "Refunds are available" in mock.calls[0]["user"] def test_answer_question_from_chunks_without_chunks(): answer = answer_question_from_chunks( question="What is the policy?", chunks=[], client=MockLLMClient(), ) assert "No document chunks" in answer def test_inspect_retrieval_returns_context(): chunks = [ "Python is useful for automation.", "Refunds are available within 30 days.", ] context = inspect_retrieval( question="refund policy", chunks=chunks, top_k=1, ) assert "Refunds" in context Test result: Python syntax check passed.

4.20 How the Code Works

This project has five main stages.

Stage 1: Load the PDF

The app asks for a PDF path.

text = load_pdf_text(pdf_path)

The pdf_loader.py file extracts text and adds page labels.

Example:

[Page 1] This document explains the refund policy... Not executed automatically: requires live API credentials, network access, or external service.

Page labels help later when you want better source tracking.

Stage 2: Split Text into Chunks

The app splits the full text into smaller chunks.

chunks = chunk_text(text)

Chunking makes retrieval more focused.

Instead of sending the full document to the model, the app sends only selected chunks.

Stage 3: Retrieve Relevant Chunks

When the user asks a question, the app retrieves chunks.

relevant_chunks = retrieve_relevant_chunks( question=question, chunks=chunks, top_k=4, )

This chapter uses keyword overlap.

If the question includes words like:

refund policy days

chunks containing those words receive higher scores.

Stage 4: Build a RAG Prompt

The retrieved chunks become context.

context = format_context(relevant_chunks) prompt = build_rag_prompt(question, context)

The prompt tells the model:

Use only the document context. If the answer is not present, say you could not find it. Do not invent facts.

Stage 5: Generate the Answer

The app calls the LLM client.

answer = llm.complete( system=RAG_SYSTEM_PROMPT, user=prompt, )

The model returns an answer based on the retrieved context.

4.21 Sample User Session

A typical session may look like this:

Personal Document AI Assistant ================================================== Ask questions about a PDF document. Type /exit to quit. Type /inspect [question] to see retrieved context. ================================================== Enter path to PDF file: sample_docs/company_policy.pdf Loading PDF... Document preview: -------------------------------------------------- [Page 1] Company Policy Manual Refunds are available within 30 days... -------------------------------------------------- Loaded 12 chunk(s). Question: What is the refund period? Assistant: Answer: The document says refunds are available within 30 days. Evidence: The retrieved context states that customers may request refunds within 30 days. Limitations: This answer is based only on the retrieved context.

This is sample output only.

Do not claim exact output unless you run the code and capture the real result.

4.22 Inspecting Retrieval

The /inspect command is important.

Try:

/inspect What is the refund period?

The app shows retrieved context before asking the model to answer.

This helps you debug RAG problems.

If the retrieved chunks are bad, the answer will probably be bad.

Do not blame the model first.

Check retrieval.

A good RAG developer asks:

Did the app retrieve the right context?

before asking:

Why did the model answer badly?

4.23 Testing the Project

Run:

pytest

Expected type of result:

20 passed

The exact number and timing may vary if you add more tests.

These tests check:

  • Text cleaning
  • Chunking
  • Preview generation
  • Tokenization
  • Chunk scoring
  • Retrieval
  • Context formatting
  • RAG prompt building
  • Mock LLM calls

The tests do not call the live model API.

That is intentional.

You should test retrieval and prompt logic without spending credits.

4.24 Live API Testing

After adding your API key to .env, run:

python app.py

Use a PDF with real selectable text.

Ask:

What is this document about?

Then ask a specific question:

What does the document say about deadlines?

Then ask an unanswerable question:

What does the document say about quantum computing?

If the document does not mention quantum computing, the assistant should say something like:

I could not find that in the document.

This is a critical RAG behavior.

A RAG assistant that cannot say “not found” is not reliable.

4.25 Why RAG Answers Can Still Be Wrong

RAG improves grounding, but it is not perfect.

Failures can happen because:

  • PDF text extraction failed
  • Chunking split important context
  • Retrieval selected the wrong chunks
  • The question was vague
  • The answer was not in the document
  • The prompt was too loose
  • The model ignored instructions
  • The document itself was unclear
  • Multiple chunks conflicted

This is why RAG apps need inspection, evaluation, and guardrails.

You will build more of those layers later.

4.26 Improving the RAG Prompt

A weak RAG prompt says:

Answer the question using this context.

A stronger RAG prompt says:

Use only the provided context. If the answer is not in the context, say you could not find it. Do not invent facts. Return answer, evidence, and limitations.

The stronger prompt gives:

  • Source boundary
  • Refusal rule
  • Output structure
  • Uncertainty handling

This improves reliability.

4.27 Chunk Size Tips

There is no perfect chunk size for every document.

Small chunks:

  • Are focused
  • May miss surrounding context

Large chunks:

  • Preserve context
  • May include irrelevant text

A reasonable beginner starting point:

chunk_size=1000 overlap=150

Try different values.

For short documents:

chunk_size=700 overlap=100

For longer technical documents:

chunk_size=1200 overlap=200

Always inspect retrieval results.

4.30 Common Mistakes

Mistake 1: Sending the Entire Document Every Time

This can be slow, expensive, and unfocused.

Retrieve relevant chunks instead.

Mistake 2: Ignoring Bad PDF Extraction

If extraction fails, the model cannot answer correctly.

Always preview extracted text.

Mistake 3: Never Inspecting Retrieved Context

If retrieval is bad, answers will be bad.

Use /inspect.

Mistake 4: Letting the Model Guess

Your prompt should say:

If the answer is not in the context, say you could not find it.

Mistake 5: Treating RAG as Perfect

RAG reduces hallucinations but does not eliminate them.

Important answers still need review.

Mistake 6: Using Poor Chunk Sizes

Bad chunking can break retrieval.

Experiment and inspect.

Mistake 7: Forgetting Source Metadata

This chapter includes page labels in extracted text.

In stronger RAG apps, store source file, page number, and chunk ID separately.

4.31 Best Practices

Preview extracted text.

Split documents into chunks.

Use overlap between chunks.

Retrieve only relevant chunks.

Inspect retrieval results.

Use strict RAG prompts.

Tell the model not to invent answers.

Make the model say “not found” when needed.

Show evidence or limitations.

Test answerable and unanswerable questions.

Review important outputs manually.
